source.citation: TowerPro, MG90S datasheet, Specifications: 'Stall torque: 1.8 kgfcm (4.8V)'. Converted at 1 kgf-cm = 0.0980665 N-m exactly (standard gravity), so 1.8 x 0.0980665 = 0.1765197. The source figure carries two significant figures; the digits beyond that are the exact conversion, not measured precision.

TowerPro, MG90S datasheet, Specifications: 'Stall torque: ... 2.2 kgfcm (6 V)'. Converted at 1 kgf-cm = 0.0980665 N-m exactly, so 2.2 x 0.0980665 = 0.2157463. CONFLICT: TowerPro's own product page prints the same 2.2 figure against 6.6V while its speed row on the same page says 6.0V. 6.0 is recorded here because the datasheet PDF and the page's own speed row agree on it; the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved. See note.

TowerPro, MG90S datasheet: 'Operating voltage: 4.8 V - 6.0 V'. CONFLICT: TowerPro's product page states 'Operating voltage: 4.8V' with no upper bound. 4.8 is recorded as nominal because both documents contain it. stall_current_a is ABSENT because neither document publishes it - sizing a supply from a figure nobody stated is the failure this schema's own description warns about.

TowerPro MG90S. Two TowerPro-attributable documents were read and they disagree with each other; both are cited per field. Neither publishes a continuous torque rating, a stall current, a gear ratio, or a feedback type, so those are absent rather than estimated.

note:
NOT THE PART IN robot 'pan-tilt-mg90s'. That build uses unbranded clones, recorded separately as `mg90s-clone-unbranded` with no torque figure at all (ADR-0024). This record is a correct account of TowerPro's published figures and describes a different product. Point 4 below anticipated exactly this and it turned out to be the case.

Four things a reader of this record needs, none of which fit in a numeric field.

1. NO CONTINUOUS RATING EXISTS. TowerPro publishes stall torque and stops, so continuous_torque_nm is null and any static capacity derived from this actuator answers incomplete (ADR-0004). This is the second vendor to do it after ROBOTIS, and unlike ROBOTIS, TowerPro does not even name the distinction. Do not take a fraction of stall.

2. OPERATING SPEED IS DELIBERATELY NOT RECORDED. The datasheet says 'Operating speed: 0.1 s/60 degree (4.8 V), 0.08 s/60 degree (6 V)' and never qualifies it as no-load. Writing it into no_load_speed_rad_s would assert something the source does not say - the same substitution ADR-0004 refuses between stall and continuous - so the figures are kept here as prose and the field is absent. If a source states the loading condition, they can be converted (0.1 s/60 deg = 10.4719755 rad/s, 0.08 s/60 deg = 13.0899694 rad/s).

3. THE TWO DOCUMENTS DISAGREE ON BODY LENGTH BY 7 MM. The product page gives 22.8 x 12.2 x 28.5 mm; the datasheet PDF gives 22.5 x 12 x 35.5 mm approx. They also disagree on dead band width (1 us against 5 us) and on whether the operating voltage has an upper bound. A servo bracket CANNOT be designed from either figure - measure the unit in hand. This is why no dimension from these documents appears in any link record.

4. THE PART IS HEAVILY CLONED, WHICH IS AN ADR-0018 BASIS PROBLEM. These figures describe TowerPro's population. An unbranded MG90S from a multipack is a different population and these numbers do not describe it, however identical the label looks. If the unit on the bench is not a verified TowerPro, this record is cited for the wrong thing.

Travel is recorded as +/- pi/2 rad from the datasheet's 'Servo can rotate approximately 180 degrees (90 in each direction)'. Note the hedge is the vendor's own word. Actuator travel is not a joint limit: the robot record's limits are what the MECHANISM permits, and a derivation takes the tighter of the two (ADR-0012).
